newsitem.title: USA: Enron, Ore. re-work merger review schedule.
newsitem.headline: Enron, Ore. re-work merger review schedule.

text.p: Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co continued talks with staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission on a new schedule for review of the companies' proposed merger, but no further formal settlement talks are planned, Enron said Thursday.
The sides met Wednesday in Salem, Ore., to work out a settlement, but failed to come to agreement on a rate cut amount for Oregon electricity customers.
"We feel we have put an incredibly beneficial offer on the table. We still want this merger to go through," said Gary Foster, a spokesman for Enron in Houston.
He said there is "always a likelihood" of informal talks resuming, but "I would not place any bets on anything fruitful coming out of it."
Enron's standing offer is for a rate cut of $61 million, including $9 million per year for four years in cost of service reductions.
The commission staff, however, is holding out for a cut of $141 million, including the same $9 million for four years in cost savings.
During Wednesday's negotiations, Enron informally offered a figure "significantly" higher than $61 million, but the staff rejected it and the proposal was withdrawn, Foster said.
Talks are now centering on whether a pre-hearing conference should be scheduled, and if so whether the commission staff needs to prepare a final report.
Enron has sought to schedule the pre-hearing conference amid expectations that a full commission hearing will be needed to clear up several aspects of the merger review.
Under a tentative schedule proposed by the staff on Wednesday, which did not include a full commission hearing, a final order was set for June 4.
The addition of the hearing process would add about two months to that timeframe, Foster said.
Talks on the schedule will likely conclude late Thursday or Friday, he added.
